prompt: Architectural revision experiment. Independently resolve the existing roof/occupied-space conflict, excessive stair rises and blocked circulation using supported operations, preserving the intended architectural character and accommodation. You may revise roof footprints, elevations, allocations, circulation or relevant geometry. Choose the geometric solution yourself. Return a separate unapproved candidate and explain your selected solution and reasons explicitly in architecturalPlan and summary. Correct programme references against final construction. Disclose unresolved and new limitations. Original brief (retained knowledge.query): Design an extraordinary $25m contemporary tropical waterfront mansion in Saint Lucia, on a flat site. Create a sophisticated luxury residence with a distinctive entrance, beautiful living spaces, private bedroom wings, purposeful upper-level architecture where appropriate, and integrated outdoor living. Choose a coherent architectural concept using relevant knowledge and construction capabilities. The result should feel like a remarkable luxury estate, not a basic bungalow. Construct fully editable direct-scene architecture.

architecturalPlan.scaleRationale: The US$25m figure is treated as a qualitative ambition reference in assumed USD, not as a formula for area, construction cost, or valuation; the resulting estate is deliberately substantial but organized as a precise waterfront compound rather than indiscriminate bulk. On the required flat Y=0 site, the architecture uses a large shared salon, two independent private pavilions, an upper owner retreat, pool court, and open lounge to create estate-level richness.
architecturalPlan.arrivalAndCirculation: Arrival is staged across the limestone pool-side approach to the framed salon entry, with public living and outdoor entertaining on the ground datum, separate guest and family pavilions reached from the exterior court, and a constructed exterior stair ascending to the owner retreat. Service provision is spatially reserved within the dining/service pavilion but equipment and back-of-house fit-out are not represented.
architecturalPlan.volumeHierarchy: The selected concept is the 'Water Court Promenade': a long primary salon facing a pool court, flanked by lower private pavilions and crowned by a recessed upper owner suite, chosen over a dispersed bungalow composition because it establishes a memorable sectional procession without inventing terrain. The salon is the dominant datum; the guest/family pavilions, pavilion lounge, entry canopy, and stair landing are subordinate elements.
architecturalPlan.relationshipsAndViews: The salon’s glazed waterfront face opens directly to the terrace and pool route, while the upper retreat looks across the same court; the family pavilion remains set back west of the principal room and the dining/service pavilion is held apart to the east. The open elliptical lounge sits beside, rather than over, the pool deck for shaded outdoor gathering.
architecturalPlan.roofFacadeAndMaterials: Ivory enclosure, limestone walking surfaces, bronze-framed openings, timber screens, broad flat roof planes, and an intentionally low secondary roofline form a deep, shade-oriented tropical identity. Flat roofs have explicit overhang geometry and the upper suite is set back beneath a separate roof; the materials express an architectural palette only and do not certify coastal performance.

programme.name: Great salon, dining and kitchen
programme.strategy: Primary ground-level salon opens through its central glazed entry bay to the waterfront terrace; dining/kitchen use is an open-plan allocation within the same constructed shell.
programme.limitation: No internal kitchen fixtures, partitions, or separately enclosed dining room are represented.

programme.name: Family bedroom pavilion
programme.strategy: Independent west pavilion uses a screened pool-facing entry bay and remains outside the principal arrival line.
programme.limitation: Bedrooms and bathrooms are programme allocations within the one-storey shell; internal partitions are not built.

programme.name: Guest bedroom pavilion
programme.strategy: East pavilion is separate from the owner suite and has its own pool-court entrance for guest privacy.
programme.limitation: Guest sleeping and bath subdivisions are not modeled.

programme.name: Upper owner suite
programme.strategy: A recessed upper shell rises over the salon and is reached from the constructed exterior stair and landing; its broad rear glazing faces the water court.
programme.limitation: The suite is a single open enclosure; dressing and bath rooms are not partitioned.

programme.name: Pool terrace and water court
programme.strategy: A continuous limestone terrace advances from the salon to the explicitly constructed rectangular pool assembly and its dry circuit.
programme.limitation: The pool assembly represents basin, coping, dry circuit, and water surface only; no hydraulic edge, filtration, excavation, or drainage is claimed.

programme.name: Open pool lounge
programme.strategy: A curved open lounge is placed beside the pool court as a sheltered social destination, not as enclosed accommodation.
programme.limitation: The approved pavilion component contains its own fixed open lounge geometry and is not subdividable.

programme.name: Arrival threshold
programme.strategy: A broad limestone approach terminates at the salon’s central operable glazed entry beneath a framed canopy.
programme.limitation: Vehicle driveway, gate, and site boundary are not modeled.

programme.name: Exterior stair and upper landing
programme.strategy: Ten progressively rising solid stair treads make a direct exterior route from the pool terrace to the supported upper landing and suite door.
programme.limitation: The stair is manually composed from solid steps; guard compliance, handrails, and accessibility compliance are not verified.
